**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination — Lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT 63030)**
**Member:** Skyler Foster
**Member ID:** W718345521
**Reference number:** POC-BDD7B46260-11524
**Date of denial notice:** August 22, 2026
**Governing policy:** 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines for Medical Necessity Review — Musculoskeletal Surgery (Lumbar Spine Surgery, CG 1766), https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the lower back disc surgery (decompression, CPT 63030) recommended by my surgeon, Dr. Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery. The denial notice dated August 22, 2026 states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision, because the records already in my file match the plan's own published criteria — including the imaging criterion the denial appears to rest on.

I am quoting below only from the plan's own guideline, the 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines for Medical Necessity Review — Musculoskeletal Surgery (Lumbar Spine Surgery, CG 1766), and then showing what my records state.

**1. The imaging criterion — the reason given for the denial**

The plan's guideline states:

> "Imaging studies showing evidence of inter-vertebral disc herniation that correlate exactly with the individual's symptoms/signs"

My MRI of the lumbar spine dated June 15, 2026 shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. My symptoms and exam findings are on the same side and at the same level: I have radicular pain into my right calf, positive provocative testing on the affected side, and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. This is the correlation the plan's own criterion asks for — imaged compression of a specific nerve root on the right, with right-sided radicular symptoms and a matching exam finding. I respectfully ask the plan to identify what, specifically, it found lacking in this correlation.

**2. Radicular symptoms that interfere with daily activities**

> "Primary radicular symptoms noted upon clinical exam that significantly hinders daily activities"

My records document radicular pain into the right calf, positive provocative testing on the affected side, and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. Functionally, I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes. I have had 18 months of progressive low back pain that is not relieved by rest.

**3. Failure of conservative treatment**

> "Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months;"

I completed supervised physical therapy from May 11, 2026 to July 20, 2026 — 10 weeks, 20 visits — including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, documented in my physical therapy discharge note. That exceeds the six-week minimum the plan states, and it falls within the last six months.

The guideline also states:

> "Non-operative conservative treatment should include a multimodality approach consisting of at least one (1) active and one (1) inactive component targeting the affected spinal region."

My care included both. The active component was supervised physical therapy with core stabilization and lumbar flexibility exercises. The inactive components were NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief and a corticosteroid injection on May 23, 2026, which gave only about 4 weeks of partial relief. All of it targeted my lumbar spine.

**4. The outcome of that treatment**

The guideline lists, among the ways this element can be met:

> "Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment; OR"

> "Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment; OR"

My records describe 18 months of progressive pain unrelieved by rest, NSAIDs with inadequate relief, and an injection that helped only partially and only for about four weeks. After completing a full 10-week course of supervised therapy, I still cannot stand for more than 10 minutes and still have radicular pain into my right calf. I am not relying on the alternative pathways in the guideline — "Documentation of a medical reason the member is unable to participate in treatment" — because I did not miss treatment. I completed it. For the same reason, the guideline's caution that "Closure of medical or therapy offices, patient inconvenience, or noncompliance without explanation does not constitute 'inability to complete' treatment" does not apply to my file.

Regarding home exercise, the guideline calls for:

> "Documentation of an exercise prescription/plan provided by a physician, physical therapist, or chiropractor; AND"

> "Follow-up documentation regarding completion of HEP after the required 6-week timeframe or inability to complete HEP due to a documented medical reason (i.e., increased pain or inability to physically perform exercises)"

My physical therapy course was supervised and was documented in a discharge note at the end of 20 visits over 10 weeks. If the plan needs a separate home exercise prescription or a home exercise follow-up note beyond that discharge documentation, I ask that the plan tell me so in writing and give my physical therapist and surgeon the opportunity to supply it, rather than denying the surgery on that basis.

**5. Surgical plan and supporting records**

> "In order for surgeries to be considered medically necessary there must be clear medical records that demonstrate a clear surgical plan that matches the request for surgery."

> "All appropriate supporting documentation, including recent pertinent office visit notes, laboratory data, and results of any special testing must be provided."

The requested procedure is a decompression at the level the MRI identifies, recommended by Dr. Duval. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed. The prior authorization packet included my clinical summary, the MRI report of June 15, 2026, my physical therapy discharge note, and my medication and injection history. My records also note no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and that I am a non-smoker. If any specific document is missing from the plan's file, I ask to be told which one so it can be sent.

**6. One point I want to be transparent about**

The guideline excerpt I have includes the sentence:

> "Microdiscectomy may be used as the first line of treatment (no conservative treatment required) in the following clinical scenarios:"

and one such scenario:

> "Progressive nerve compression resulting in an acute neurologic deficit (motor) due to herniated disc. The neurological deficits should be significant: 0-2/5 on the motor function scale for L5 or S1 roots OR 0-3/5 for L3 or L4 roots. Lesser degrees of motor dysfunction may resolve with conservative treatment and are not considered an indication for early surgery"

I am **not** basing my appeal on that early-surgery pathway, and I am not claiming any particular motor score — my records state a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level without giving a grade. I am basing my appeal on the standard pathway, because I completed more than the six weeks of conservative care the plan requires. I also want to note that the sentence above introduces a list of further clinical scenarios that I was not given the full text of, and that the excerpts I have may not be the complete set of criteria the plan applied. Beyond the excerpts quoted above, I have not quoted the plan's policy, and I am not characterizing any criteria I have not seen.

**What I am asking for**

I ask that the plan overturn the denial dated August 22, 2026 (reference POC-BDD7B46260-11524) and authorize CPT 63030 as recommended by Dr. Duval. If the plan upholds the denial, I ask that it provide in writing:

1. the specific criterion or criteria from CG 1766 that my records were found not to meet;
2. the specific finding the reviewer expected in the imaging and did not find, given the MRI's description of L4-L5 disc extrusion with compression of the traversing right L5 nerve root and my matching right-sided symptoms and exam;
3. the credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made the determination; and
4. a complete copy of the criteria applied, including any portions not reproduced in the excerpts above.

I understand my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the denial notice, by **February 18, 2027**. I am submitting this appeal in writing to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I am available at the phone number above if the reviewer would like to discuss my case or needs anything further from Dr. Duval's office or my physical therapist. If this appeal is not decided in my favor, I ask that I be told in writing what further appeal or review rights are available to me and what time limits apply to them.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at my records.

Sincerely,

**Skyler Foster**
